questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms.

(i) Copulation.

(ii) Ovulation.

(iii) Fertilization. *(3, 3, 4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Copulation** (sexual intercourse, mating) is the **act in which the erect penis of the male is placed in the vagina of the female and semen containing sperms is ejaculated into the vagina**, so that sperms can reach the egg. It is a form of internal fertilisation.

(ii) **Ovulation** is the **release of a mature egg cell (ovum, secondary oocyte) from the Graafian follicle of the ovary into the funnel of the oviduct (Fallopian tube)**. It occurs about **day 14** of a 28-day menstrual cycle, under the influence of luteinising hormone (LH).

(iii) **Fertilization** is the **fusion of the nucleus of a male gamete (sperm) with the nucleus of a female gamete (ovum) to form a diploid zygote**. In humans it takes place in the **upper part of the oviduct (Fallopian tube)**. The zygote then divides by mitosis and is implanted in the uterus wall.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe the process of birth in humans. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Birth (parturition) occurs at the end of pregnancy, about **9 months (38 to 40 weeks)** after fertilisation. It is controlled by hormones: the level of **progesterone falls** and the **posterior pituitary gland releases oxytocin**, which makes the **uterine muscles contract**.

**Stage 1 - Labour and dilation of the cervix:** the muscular wall of the uterus starts to contract rhythmically (labour pains), slowly at first and then more often and strongly. The **cervix (neck of the uterus) widens (dilates)**. The **amnion (amniotic sac) breaks** and the **amniotic fluid** flows out through the vagina ("the waters break"). The baby normally lies **head down**.

**Stage 2 - Delivery of the baby:** stronger contractions of the uterus, helped by the contraction of the abdominal muscles (the mother pushes), force the baby **head first** through the dilated cervix and the vagina to the outside. The **umbilical cord** is then **clamped, tied and cut**; the baby usually cries, which fills its lungs with air and starts breathing. The remaining cord shrivels and forms the navel (umbilicus).

**Stage 3 - Afterbirth:** within about 10 to 30 minutes, further contractions of the uterus **expel the placenta and the foetal membranes (afterbirth)**. The uterus then contracts and gradually returns to its normal size. The mother needs rest, and breast feeding (colostrum) begins.

questions.enonce_markdown: State two functions of the placenta. *(2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two:
1. The placenta allows the **exchange of materials between the mother's blood and the foetus's blood**: **oxygen, glucose, amino acids, mineral salts, vitamins and antibodies pass to the foetus**, while **carbon dioxide and urea (excretory wastes) pass from the foetus to the mother**.
2. It **secretes hormones (progesterone and oestrogen)** which maintain the pregnancy.
3. It acts as a **barrier** that protects the foetus from many harmful substances and micro-organisms and prevents mixing of the mother's and the foetus's blood.
